A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Video-Oasis study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic results across 14 benchmarks, model evaluations, filtering analyses, and temporal-grounding and reasoning ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds diagnostic-model and category-annotation robustness comparisons.

M1.justification: The visual and temporal diagnostic tests, consensus filtering, human verification, and category-labeling procedure are retained. Narrative becomes Summary, while the added annotation prompts document the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14 benchmarks, five challenge categories, and ImplicitQA/KFS-Bench oracle-grounding scenario. Revised sample counts and additional model configurations do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A adds MiMo-VL-SFT, LLaVA-Video, and VideoLLaMA3 to the Center-Frame and Frame Shuffling comparisons. Appendix D.3 adds alternative annotation ensembles. The main Table 7 comparator set is retained; VideoTool and STAR reference the same work.

E3.justification: The reported filtered evaluation set changes from 11,332 QA pairs and 5,199 videos to 11,033 pairs and 4,938 videos. Additional diagnostic and annotation ensemble configurations are evaluated. Core frame budgets and diagnostic settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain whether the sample-count revisions reflect corrections or reselection.

E4.justification: v2 extends diagnostic-model sensitivity analysis and adds a focused test of category-label stability across alternative annotator ensembles. The main grounding and reasoning ablations remain. The difficulty-baseline analysis moves from v1 Appendix A.1 to Section 4.1; v1's extended shortcut examples in Figure S6 are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies and overlaps without repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. The additional model-ensemble comparisons do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The overall filtering ratio changes from 53.6% to 54.8%, with revised benchmark and category counts. New shortcut-overlap results span 87.5–88.6%, and new annotation-overlap results span 93.2–95.8%. Table 11 changes Qwen2.5-VL accuracy from 29.1 to 29.2; Figure 1(c) also revises Eagle2.5's original-set score and gap. Most retained accuracy tables and rankings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C's equations and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content. Renaming the consensus threshold from k to c changes notation only. No new theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the headline shortcut-prevalence claim from 54% to 55%. The central contributions remain benchmark auditing, identifying video-native challenges, and deriving algorithmic guidelines.

C2.justification: The new Discussion acknowledges that captions and shuffled frames can preserve temporal cues and cause false positives or negatives. Sections 3.3 and C.1 also soften interpretations of shortcut validity and caption-based success, replacing stronger assertions with more qualified diagnostic conclusions.

D1.justification: Tables S15–S16 disclose taxonomy-construction and category-assignment prompts, including annotation inputs and text-only labeling. Section 4.2 clarifies that overall accuracy aggregates all samples. Conversely, v1's explicit human majority-vote rule is omitted. The code-access statement and core implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MiMo-VL, VideoLLaMA3, and LLaVA-Video and removes VideoEval-Pro. Positioning relative to EgoTempo, Cambrian-S, and Apollo remains substantively consistent, with clearer explanation of the diagnostic axes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, diagnostic explanations, and substantial portions of the experimental narrative are rewritten. Terminology is standardized, the difficulty-baseline discussion moves into the main text, and Appendix D.3 is repurposed for annotation documentation. This is extensive editorial restructuring despite a stable core method.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised, including headings and benchmark-axis ordering; other captions and labels are refined. Appendix Table S1 is expanded and rearranged, new overlap and prompt tables are added, and Figure S6 is removed. Most existing figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Additional robustness checks, explicit annotation prompts, and clearer diagnostic limitations improve evidential support and transparency. The gains are limited by the largely unchanged main evaluation. Removed shortcut examples and human-voting detail, together with unexplained filtered-set revisions alongside retained accuracy tables, temper the improvement.
